8f667fad308958148993c84ef063203eeff24752.summary:
The recipe box app is built. It's a single self-contained `index.html` with no dependencies, ready to preview in a browser.

What it includes, mapped to the plan:

- **Recipe input form** — paste any recipe text free-form with a name and tags. If you skip the name, it auto-grabs the first line of the pasted text as the title.
- **Tag system** — comma-separated tags on entry, rendered as a clickable tag cloud with counts. Filters combine (AND logic) and stack with a live full-text search box; a Clear button resets both.
- **Spinning picker as the hero** — the "Spin for Dinner!" button sits front and center. It rapidly flips through recipe names with an easing slowdown (like a wheel losing momentum), then pops the winner card with a burst of ingredient confetti (🧄🥕🌿). The spinner respects your active filters, so you can filter to "weeknight" and spin within just those. A "peek at the recipe" link opens the full recipe.
- **Warm kitchen aesthetic** — cream and terracotta palette with sage and butter accents, Georgia serif typography, a gingham border strip up top, dashed "recipe card" borders, and cozy microcopy throughout ("Tuck it in the box").
- **Persistence** — everything saves to localStorage and survives reloads. On first visit it seeds two starter recipes (tomato orzo, chicken soup) so the spinner works immediately; deleting them is remembered too.

Recipes open in a modal for full reading, with delete (confirmation-guarded) available there. Empty states and no-match-filter states are both handled, and the layout collapses to a single column on mobile.

45d6ce9cf3197267dbb1d05025e5fdaa48d74ee0.summary:
Theming is in. The app now has a 🎨 theme button pinned to the top-right corner that opens a dropdown with five themes, each shown with three color swatch dots and a checkmark on the active one: **Cozy Kitchen** (the original warm terracotta look), **Midnight Snack** (a dark mode), **Herb Garden** (greens), **Seaside Supper** (blues with a sandy accent), and **Berry Patch** (pinks).

How it works:

- The whole stylesheet already ran on CSS custom properties, so each theme is just a `[data-theme="..."]` block that overrides the palette. I also moved the remaining hard-coded colors (the gingham border, body glow gradients, button text, winner card, modal overlay, danger button, tag colors) into variables so every theme recolors the entire app, including the dark theme's inverted text.
- Picking a theme sets `data-theme` on `<html>` and saves the choice to localStorage; a tiny script in `<head>` re-applies it before first paint so there's no flash of the default theme on reload.
- The menu closes on outside click or Escape, the toggle button shows the current theme's name (icon-only on small screens), and background/panel colors cross-fade over 0.3s when switching.

Everything else — the spinner, filters, modal, and saved recipes — is untouched and works as before.

Apply everything branch 'feat/neon' built onto the current app. Preserve the current app's behavior wherever the branch did not touch it; where they conflict, blend sensibly in favor of the branch's intent.

## Vibes on the branch (oldest first)
- Restyle the whole app as neon cyberpunk — near-black background, glowing magenta/cyan accents, monospace headings, subtle scanline texture. Keep every existing feature working exactly as before.

## The branch's distilled prompt (describes the branch's finished app)

Build a recipe box app where users paste and organize recipes with tags, then spin a button to get random dinner suggestions.

**Recipe Input**: A form to add recipes by pasting text (ingredients, steps, links, notes). Users enter a recipe name or it auto-guesses from the first non-empty line of pasted text. Tags are comma-separated (e.g., "weeknight, soup, vegetarian"). Recipes save to localStorage automatically.

**Recipe Display**: Cards in a scrollable list showing recipe name, 2-line text preview, and tag chips. Clicking any card opens a modal with the full recipe text, all tags, and a delete button. Seed the app on first visit with two starter recipes (One-Pot Tomato Orzo and Lazy Sunday Chicken Soup).

**Tag Cloud & Filtering**: Display all tags with recipe counts. Users can click tags to filter (AND logic—selecting "soup" and "weeknight" shows only recipes with both). A search box filters by recipe name, text content, or tags. Show a "Clear" button when filters are active. Display a count line ("3 recipes in the box" or "Showing 2 of 5").

**The Spinner Hero**: A "Spin for Dinner!" button with a 🥘 icon in a prominent hero section. Clicking it picks a random recipe from the filtered list (or all recipes if no filters). The button animates through recipe names with easing-out delays, then reveals the winner in a card with a "peek at the recipe" link and confetti (🧄 🧅 🥕 🌿 🧂 🍅 ✨) falling.

**Neon Cyberpunk Design**:
- **Background**: Near-black void (#07070e, #0d0d1a layers) with subtle radial gradients (magenta/cyan glow at edges)
- **Colors**: Neon magenta (#ff2ec4), cyan (#00f0ff), violet (#8a5cff), soft gray text (#d8e0f0)
- **Typography**: Monospace (Courier New) for headings/labels, sans-serif for body
- **Effects**: Glowing text-shadows on titles, neon box-shadows around panels, CRT scanline texture overlay (subtle repeating horizontal lines)
- **Accents**: Neon top strip (magenta-violet-cyan gradient with heavy glow), glowing borders on input fields and cards
- **Interactive**: Buttons glow brighter on hover, cards have colored left borders (cyan/magenta/violet alternating)
- **Animations**: Title flickers subtly, spinner button rotates continuously while spinning, winner card pops with overshoot easing, confetti falls with rotation

**Technical Details**:
- Single-file HTML/CSS/JS app (no build step)
- localStorage for persistence (key: "recipe-box-v1")
- Vanilla JS (no frameworks)
- Graceful empty states with helpful emoji & text
- Modal overlay with ESC-to-close and click-outside-to-close
- Responsive design for mobile and desktop (two-column layout becomes single column on mobile)
